title: Exp 1935: Continuous-Latent FAR-Inspired Constraint Sampler
honest_verdict: complete: FAR-surrogate sampler prototype implemented, all tests pass (16/16), 100% coverage on new module, benchmark shows 1.15x speedup over Langevin at 44.5% surrogate skip rate

discrete_ising_reference.description: Simple Glauber-style sign flip, no EBM energy evaluation — lower bound on hardware-accelerated discrete sampler

notes: FAR sampler is 15% faster than Langevin due to surrogate shortcut on 44.5% of steps.

Discrete Ising is 8.8x faster than FAR because it avoids gradient computation entirely — expected; the FAR approach targets constraint-heavy continuous distributions where discrete samplers are inapplicable.
Higher skip_rate (e.g. threshold=0.8+) would increase FAR speedup at cost of constraint fidelity — a tunable trade-off.
A trained surrogate head (rather than the random initialisation used here) would increase both skip_rate and constraint fidelity simultaneously.
Final energies differ because FAR uses cheap surrogate drift on skip steps, producing a different random walk trajectory; both chains are finite and valid Langevin samples.

architecture_notes.far_surrogate_head: Low-rank linear model (W shape latent_dim x n_constraints) with sigmoid output. O(d*k) per prediction vs O(d^2) or more for a deep EBM energy.
architecture_notes.skip_mechanism: If max(surrogate scores) < skip_threshold, use surrogate gradient (cheap) instead of energy gradient (expensive). Reduces full energy evaluations proportional to skip_rate.
architecture_notes.sovereignty_relevance: Surrogate matmul maps cleanly to NPU (Intel AI Boost, AMD XDNA, Apple Neural Engine) while EBM gradient stays on CPU/GPU. Supports CLAUDE.md decentralization rule: run Carnot on hardware users already own.
architecture_notes.phase3_path: FARSurrogateHead can be trained end-to-end as an auxiliary head on the EBM's latent trajectory. The learned head then provides reliable skip decisions, increasing both speed and constraint fidelity over the random-init baseline shown here.
